name: agent_events
description: What an agent has actually been doing — its most recent events, oldest first.

name: agent_list
description: Launched runs owned by this conversation, including nested children; not the agent roster.

name: agent_providers
description: Which agent CLIs can be spawned here, and which named agents each can resolve.

name: agent_send
description: Send a message to another agent — it answers with its full context intact.

name: agent_spawn
description: Start an agent to work alongside you, or hand the task to the idle one of that role already in this conversation (`fresh` to always start one), and return its run id immediately.

name: agent_stop
description: Stop a running agent (and the tool processes it spawned), or take one not started yet out of the line.

name: audit_ui
description: Drive every interactive element through its own states and report MEASURED anomalies — no vision model, no opinion. A still screenshot cannot show a menu that closed the instant the pointer moved toward it, a tray covering its own trigger, focus that vanished, or a page that shifted when something opened; this catches exactly that class by actually hovering, focusing, pressing, opening and closing each control and comparing real geometry / hit-testing / focus / accessible-name / text-fit / settle-time before and after.

name: community_search
description: Search the community library — agents, skills and prompts published by people or imported from public repositories under their licence — for one made for `need` (a few words: « reverse engineer a binary », « write release notes »). Lists the best matches (id, kind, title, what it is for, source and licence) and the repositories listed by link only. Start one with agent_spawn(community=<id>, task=...): it runs as your child, under your control.

name: conversation_read
description: Read one conversation this computer holds, `limit` lines at a time (what was asked, answered, said between agents, each tool call by its leading argument; never tool output; credentials masked).

name: conversation_search
description: Search the conversations this computer holds — the runs galaius started and the sessions each agent CLI saved (the person's editor conversations) — for every word of `query`.

name: create_file
description: Write a file the person opens — a document, a spreadsheet, a deck, a PDF, a mail draft — in your working folder.

name: download_asset
description: Download a URL to a local file. Uses the browser session's cookies for authenticated downloads.

name: edit_video
description: Edit a video in your working folder — cut it, join clips, caption it, lay text over it, resize it, take its sound — on this PC, at no cost, and show the result in the person's chat as a video they can play and download.

name: generate_3d
description: Make a 3D model (a .glb file) of the object shown in an image, with your company's 3D model.

name: generate_image
description: Draw an image (up to 4) with your company's image model on the Galaius platform and save it here.

name: generate_music
description: Compose music from a description with your company's music model, as an audio file.

name: generate_sound
description: Make a sound effect from a description with your company's sound model, as an audio file.

name: generate_speech
description: Say a text aloud with your company's voice model, as an audio file.

name: get_interactive_elements
description: List the interactive elements with numbered badges + their details; act on them by the returned `ref`/`element` in run_actions.

name: get_logs
description: Return captured browser logs (last `limit` entries). source="network" → requests (method/status/url), source="console" → console messages + errors. clear=True flushes after reading.

name: get_page_state
description: Get current page URL, title, accessibility tree, focused element, visible text, and the page's interactive elements as a numbered `ref` list — so you can act by `ref` in run_actions immediately, no separate get_interactive_elements call needed. Refs come from a pure DOM scan (no VLM, works with any model). scope: CSS selector to restrict to a page sub-tree. tab: read a specific tab by index (like get_interactive_elements); unset = the active tab (#74).

name: launch_app
description: Launch an app in galaius's isolated sandbox display and drive it there.

name: list_desktop_windows
description: List desktop targets for the `target` param, on Linux, Windows and macOS: each monitor with its geometry (target="screen" for the whole desktop, target="screen:<index>" or "screen:<name>" for one) and each open window. On Linux target a window by its title, or — when a title isn't unique — by target="wid:<id>". On Windows / macOS windows are listed (for wait_for window=… and for screenshot region=…) but driven through the screen target.

name: list_providers
description: Return subscription visual CLIs, API/local providers, and current configuration.

name: measure_ui
description: DETERMINISTIC pixel measurement of a UI — exact colors + WCAG contrast, NO VLM (no spend, fully reproducible). Use it for a number you can trust instead of a model's guess: the contrast ratio of text vs background, the exact color at a point, or the biggest empty band on screen.

name: navigate
description: Navigate to a URL and return page content. Browser-only — requires a session, not a window.

name: record
description: Record actions as video and optionally analyze with vision.

name: report_issue
description: Report a problem, missing capability, or feedback about GALAIUS ITSELF — not the site/app you're automating — to its maintainers, so it gets fixed. Use when galaius errors in a way that blocks you, behaves unexpectedly, or is missing something you needed.

name: reset_sandbox
description: Tear down galaius's isolated sandbox display — kill every app launched into it and stop the nested X server. The next launch_app starts a fresh display.

name: review_ui
description: Capture the UI and return a STRUCTURED critique of what's WRONG with it — low-contrast or unreadable text, overflow/clipping, truncation, misalignment, broken/empty/error states, black or occluded regions, tiny tap targets, off-theme colors — so you can JUDGE a UI's quality without hand-writing a vision prompt. Use it after a change to confirm the result looks right, or to hunt defects on any screen.

name: run_actions
description: Execute a sequence of actions on a browser session or desktop window.

name: screenshot
description: Capture the current page or a desktop window.

name: session
description: Manage browser sessions — one tool for the whole lifecycle.

name: transcribe
description: Transcribe an audio (or audio-bearing) file to text, and optionally answer a question about it.

name: translate
description: Translate a text into another language with your company's text model, keeping its layout.

name: verify_ui
description: Judge a UI against your LITERAL requirements — one PASS/FAIL per requirement, each anchored to the exact element it judged. The acceptance complement to review_ui (which DISCOVERS defects): hand it the checklist a freeform critique glosses ("the coin pill shows a GOLD coin, not a flame"; "the bottom nav has exactly 4 tabs"; "the FAB does not overlap the tab bar") and it tests each to the letter — presence is not enough, the form/color/count/state must match.
